chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdallah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man from among you is asked about that which he does not know, he should say: 'I do not know,' and should not say: 'Allah is more knowing,' because that will cast doubt in the heart of the questioner; and if the questioned says: 'I do not know,' then the questioner should not blame him.
ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette for answering when you do not know the answer to a question according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith provides ethical guidance on how to respond when asked about matters one does not know. It instructs the respondent to say 'I do not know' rather than 'Allah is more knowing,' as the latter phrase can inadvertently cause the questioner to doubt the respondent's knowledge or sincerity. It also advises the questioner not to suspect or blame the respondent for their lack of knowledge.

en.ammaar-muslim: 5. [5/39] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from Hammad b. Isa from Hariz b. Abdallah from Muhammad b. Muslim from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام who said:

if a man from among you is asked about that which he does not know – he should say: “I do not know” and should not say: “Allāh is more knowing”, because that will cast doubt in the heart of the questioner, and if the questioned says: “I do not know” then the questioner should not blame him.
